newsitem.title: USA: Phoenix Duff sees no more big 1997 charges.
newsitem.headline: Phoenix Duff sees no more big 1997 charges.

text.p: Phoenix Duff & Phelps Corp does not expect any other significant non-recurring expenses that could adversely impact earnings for the remainder of 1997, Philip McLoughlin, chief executive officer, said Tuesday.

McLoughlin made the forecast as the money management firm reported net earnings for the first quarter ended March 31, 1997 of $3.759 million or $0.06 per primary share, compared with $7.113 million or $0.14 per primary share, for the prior year's period.

It said that included in 1997 earnings were two non-recurring expense items, which negatively affected earnings per share by $0.045. At the same time, 1996 earnings included a non-recurring income item which had a positive effect on earnings per share of $0.02, it said.

It said the first expense relates to the decision of a senior executive to exercise rights under his employment agreement entered into at the time of the merger of Phoenix Securities Group and Duff & Phelps Corpo in November 1995.

The second item results from a recorded loss relating to the liquidation of Windy City CBO Partners L.P., it said. In February, Windy City's portfolio was liquidated, bondholders were paid and the partnership was dissolved. As a result of the liquidation, it received $11.2 million in cash, it said.
"As we pursue and achieve our strategic goals, we will continue to focus on improving both sales and operating results," McLoughlin said.
